messages.text: you up already?
going by East Central before work. line's worse if you wait
for what lol it's not november
bond's on there and the sheriff. that bond is our taxes for the next 20 years baby. go after your shift
Pastor Wells wants the Easter supper sign-up sheet by Sunday. He asked if you'd run the whole list again.
I told him I'd circle back today. I've already got Tuesday morning blocked for the food bank rotation and Thursday for choir setup.
Honey, that's three things this week and we haven't even touched Easter. Tommy still at the shipyard all day?
Yeah, his shifts are steady. I'm home, so I can carry it. Just don't let me say yes to the prayer-chain rewrite too, ok?
Pastor Webb asked if you can take the sign-up clipboard for the Lenten suppers again. Last year you had 22 people locked in by week two.
Tell him yes but I need the printed roster by Friday. I'll split the casserole slots from the bread slots so nobody doubles up like Miss Doreen did.
I knew you'd say yes. He also wants to know if you'll handle the kitchen rotation for the after-funeral plate for the Robicheaux family Saturday.
Yes. I'll call around tonight, get four ladies on greens, two on tea, and one runner. Send me the family count so I know what to multiply.
If Eli sleeps over Saturday, do you still have that little air mattress in the closet?
I do. I keep it folded behind Tommy's tool tote in the front room.
Okay. He'll bring his own blanket and cup so you don't have to dig around.
That helps. I'll set him up after supper and put everything back Sunday.
Eli asked if you still had the little jar with the peach filling from Sunday.
I used the last spoonful in a small pan this morning. The crust held better than the one I sent home with y'all.
He said the square piece was good but the edge was crumbly. His exact words were 'too sandy.'
Tell my helper I wrote that down. Next batch gets colder butter and a little less flour.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: If Eli spends Saturday night, can you send him back with a cucumber if your back rows have any?
They are just starting, but I can send two little ones and some tomatoes if he leaves them alone.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: He will eat tomatoes in your kitchen and act like mine are poison.
I am meeting Linda for our loop by the church before choir, then I will wash a bowl for y'all.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Eli says he wants to sit by Caleb Sunday, not the grownup end.
I will put his booster by Caleb's chair and write his name on the blue cup so nobody fusses.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: You already thought of that?
Plates are counted, two pans are marked, and I am setting aside a mild piece before Tommy starts with the pepper.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Mama, Eli's clinic asked for the new card copy if you still have it in your purse.
I do. Tommy brought the fresh one home with his badge stuff Friday, so I can send you a picture after supper.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Thank you. And don't let Daddy carry that tool bag tonight if his back is still fussing.
I already told him the same. He came in smelling like dock rope and grease and still tried to fix the sink.
You still making that lemon cake Sunday or did the clinic papers ruin dessert for everybody?
I can make it, but I am sending most of it home with you. I am keeping to the fruit bowl after supper.
Fine by me. What about rolls?
Tommy can have one. I am doing greens and chicken and skipping the soft white ones this week.
You headed over early? Sister Pat wants the altos warmed up before everyone files in.
Leaving now. Bringing the folder with the new arrangement so we are not flipping pages again.
Bless you. Save me the seat at the end of the second row, my knee is acting up tonight.
Done. See you in a few.
Saw your group post about Saturday cleanup signups. I shared it to my page too.
Did you see what Sheriff Ezell put on his page about the bridge work on Highway 613?
Yeah I saw it after the WLOX piece at six. Wanted to read both before I said anything to Tommy.
Thank you. The post is doing okay but I am still short three spots for the morning shift.
Did Miss Earlene see it yet? You know she does not get on there.
Sister Pearl was telling everyone after choir that they're closing the whole stretch Monday. I couldn't find that anywhere.
No I will ring her after choir tomorrow. Same with Mr. Bobby and Sister Pat.
Hm. I'll wait until I see it on the county page before I pass that one on. She gets things half right sometimes.
You left your blue choir folder on the back pew. I grabbed it.
Thank you. I stepped outside when the back hallway got thick and must have set it down.
I figured. I saw you wave off that little pen and the plate from Kevin's cousin.
Coffee and Ms. Ann's plain pound cake were enough for me tonight.
Eli's preschool sent another form home. Are you still stopping by the clinic after Mama's grocery run?
Yes. I want to ask the nurse what dates they are putting on the school sheet before I fill his part wrong.
Good. The parent group was all over the place last night.
I am going by the clinic handout and what the pharmacist prints for mine. Less guessing.
Could Eli use the blue blanket at your place Saturday if I leave his Paw Patrol bag?
Yes, I washed it after Caleb used the couch last time. Tell him the dinosaur cup is still in the cabinet.
Perfect. He keeps asking if Uncle Caleb will save him a biscuit.
I will text Caleb after his shift and see if he is coming by Sunday.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Mama, Eli asked if Sunday lunch has the little cornbread squares again.
It can. I have meal from the cabinet, beans soaking, and eggs enough to stretch it.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Want me to bring anything from Ocean Springs?
Just him. I left those black slip-ons in the online cart and moved the Bayou Dental card off the fridge for now.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Eli's preschool packet has a family tree page. Do you remember which hospital your baby picture was from?
Mama always said the little picture was from Singing River over in Pascagoula. I still have the card tucked in the Bible.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: I'll write that. He also needs where the grandparents grew up.
Put Jackson County for my side unless they ask for town names. Moss Point, Gautier, Pascagoula... all right here.
Did you see Sandra finally put the pound cake recipe up on the choir page? Mae was begging for it after last potluck.
Saw it, copied it into my notebook. The brown sugar amount looks off though, I'll ask her Sunday before I try it.
Be ready, the comments got testy about whether March bake sale moves up a week. I closed it out and went to bed.
Yeah I scrolled past that. Not getting in the middle of Mae and Doris over dates.
Did you see the clip from the Pascagoula stop on the news? Young man got cuffed before the camera even came up.
I saw it. That officer went from zero to ten in about two seconds. If supervisors actually watched their own footage we wouldn't keep seeing the same thing.
Mhm. You think they'll do anything?
Probably not unless somebody files and they take it serious for once. Just you and me on the porch about it, like always.
Mama got out the old photo box again. The one from the Griffin Street house.
Lord. The yellow kitchen one or the back porch one?
Yellow kitchen. You in that flowered top, me behind you, Granny on the steps. Had to be 95 or 96.
Granny was staying with us that whole summer I think. Daddy was still pulling those long weeks out at the yard.
I left your little weekly box by the coffee maker.
Thank you. I need to fill the empty row tonight after choir.
That Laird paper still on the fridge for the 17th?
Yes. Just the regular check-in, then he said I should book the fall one before I leave.
Stopped at Winn-Dixie on Highway 90. Got six gallons. Want me to grab another case?
Yes please. And D batteries if they still have them. The pack from 2021 in the blue tub is mostly dead.
Got it. Filled the gas cans at Murphy too while I was out. $42.
Good. Earlier we start this year the better. Folder by the dresser needs the new insurance paper too, remind me tonight.
you tell dad we still going saturday? tide chart looks decent on the singing river side
He's planning an early launch. Bring the rod we put new line on, and grab live shrimp at the hwy 90 bait shop on your way over.
cool. cumbest bluff or you think he wants lower river by the marsh?
He said Lower if the wind stays down. Pack extra leader, last time you lost two rigs in the grass.
you ok? saw you stay after the meeting last night
yeah. Hardy talked for 22 min straight about the new pavilion bid and Miss Renata from Pecan never got to say a word about her ditch backing up
I caught her in the parking lot and asked her to write it down so I can read it at the next one if she don't want to stand up. she said ok
that's why people show up when you ask them. bless you for hanging back
I can leave Gautier after 8 if Mama's lab slip is still on the fridge.
Finish your church pantry run. I already put the slip in my purse and I'll stop for eggs after.
You say that every time. At least let me do the little blue box tonight.
Bring yourself Sunday and fuss at me then. I'll set it up while Mama eats breakfast.
paycheck hits tonight. mortgage auto pulls saturday, truck note monday
ok. the visa min is 47 i'll knock it out wednesday. balance still sitting at 2100 ish
gas tank low. can it wait till after the bills clear
yeah just put 20 in for now. we'll do a real fill saturday morning
I saved the end seat near the coffee urn for tonight. You can slip out from there easy.
Thank you. If I get busy talking, wave me down at 6:45 so I actually sit a minute.
I will. Also Raymond said he can carry the extra pans from the kitchen.
Good. I can handle the sign-in table and desserts if the heavy stuff stays off my list.
I put your alto folder in my tote so it won't get left behind again.
Thank you. I still have Miss Carol's tiny scissors in my purse from the fabric table.
She noticed. She said bring them Wednesday and she will forgive you for one peppermint.
Deal. If my phone starts buzzing before then, you may get the first ring so talk me down.
Sister Geneva put us down for the covered dish supper on the 21st. She said your peach hand pies sold out at the harvest one and she wants them again.
Mercy. I told her two trays last time and she wrote down four. Did the same again didn't she
Four. And she added you to the funeral meal rotation for Miss Earlene's family Saturday after service. I told her I'd help you wrap
Alright. Bring your big foil pans. I'll start the dough Friday night after I finish that quilt block for Marissa
snack day for Eli Wednesday, can you do the watermelon stars again? he asked specifically
yes ma'am. easy. tell that boy his grandma got him
also the new lead at his room is Ms. Brittany, real sweet. she said she did the two-year track at MGCCC nights and weekends, said they take folks any age. thought of you
send me her name and the link if you got it. I been eyeing that one for fall. need to get through May first though

messages.text: You were up when Eli came crawling in my bed? I saw your note at 3:18 about snack money.
It was just numbers running around. I wrote the school snack, light bill, and gas down so they would quit circling.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Mama, please nap before lunch. I can bring the apple slices and cups.
That helps. Once it is on paper I can breathe easier and go fix biscuits.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Eli asked if Nana has the little green crunchies again for lunch today.
Tell him I pulled two before breakfast. I can slice those with the red ones if he behaves.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: He'll behave for food. Need me to bring anything with the fish?
Just lemons if you pass the store. I clipped thyme already and washed a bowl of greens.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Eli found your beach bucket in my trunk. Want me to bring it Sunday or keep it here?
Bring it Sunday. I am still just adding little bits to that Gulf Shores envelope, so no rush.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: I can print those ferry photos from Ocean Springs too. The old bridge one looked like something you would paste in that county notebook.
Yes please. I want the ferry page beside the Pascagoula notes, then I can compare it with the map page for Dauphin Island and New Orleans.
Brenda asked again if you'd cover the booth at the candidate meet-and-greet Saturday. She said just the sign-ins.
tell her I'll do the church supper after, but I can't sit at that table. you know my rule
I told her. She said it isn't endorsing, just greeting. I said you'd still say no.
right. if I hand out one sticker I'm in it. supper hall yes, that table no. been the same answer since the kids were small
drove past the community center on Main and they had a help wanted card taped to the front door, did you see it
no but Renee mentioned hours opening up there, front desk and some afternoon program work I think. I want to ask once I have my test date locked
lock the test date first, you been talking about that paper a long time
I know I know. one thing at a time. test, then walk in there with something to hand them
Servicing letter came. Payment goes out Friday same as always.
Leave it by the coffee can. I want to compare it with the 2008 folder before I call them.
Found it in the hall closet. Same box as our courthouse paper and the kids' baby pictures.
That box has survived more storms than the porch rail has.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Mama, are you still meeting those ladies by the river or can you get Eli at 8:30?
I can get him. We finished early because that pavement was already shining.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Good, don't overdo it out there. I'll pack his blue cup.
Thank you. I was glad Linda and Cheryl showed up; I would not have stayed on that back stretch alone.
Eli's class is doing a 'what does your grandparent do' week. He wants to talk about Daddy and the trucks.
Aww. Tell him Granddaddy fixes the big stuff so the boats can keep moving. Same as your Papaw did before him.
Ha. Two generations of busted knuckles. Did Papaw ever work the same side of the yard as Daddy?
Different outfits, same kind of work. Papaw was more on the industrial side, welding repairs, that sort. Both of them came home smelling like the same shop rags though.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: Can you grab Eli at 2:45 if my appointment runs long?
That is my fabric afternoon at First Baptist. Miss Carol has me pinning borders after lunch.

messages.sender: Marissa Rubel or married surname not specified
messages.text: No worries. If something changes fast, should I try Linda instead of Tommy while he's at work?
Yes, Linda will answer, and she keeps her head clear. Text me too and I'll step out.
Mama said you called Earlene yesterday. She told Mama you talked her ear off about the river cleanup.
Had to. She is not on the page so I cannot tag her in the signup thread.
I told Mama same thing about the funeral plate sign up last month. Half of them I had to dial.
Right. The thread fills the youngers fast. The rest is the phone.
Cousin Tisha wants to know if you're riding up to Jackson Saturday for that march at the capitol.
No ma'am. Tell her I'm not the marching kind. I'll be at the bakery testing and then Mama's pills need sorting.
She's gonna fuss.
Let her. I do my part different. Officer Pritchett still waved me through when I forgot my tag last month, and the one before him talked to Caleb like he was nothing. Both can be true.
Can I stop by after shift and run a load? Mine's piled up.
Come on. Washer's free after Tommy's work shirts finish.
I might crash if I'm too tired to drive back.
I'll leave the couch sheets in the basket. Take them off before you head out in the morning.
Do you want the short side by the cemetery tomorrow or the longer loop past the fellowship hall?
Longer one. I have had a full head all afternoon and need to talk while my feet are busy.
I will be there at 7:10. Bring me one of those peppers if the little red ones are ready.
Deal. I picked a handful before supper and put them beside the sink.
Snack day pic - Eli with his apple slices. Smiling for once 🍎
Oh my goodness, those cheeks. I'm saving that one to my phone right now.
Mama did you see what Aunt Jolene put up about Cheryl and the car payment thing? It's still going.
I saw it. Closed it out and didn't say a word. Nothing good comes from me posting on a family fuss like that.
Did you call that number on the back of Tommy's card or are you waiting till after Mama's groceries?
Waiting till his lunch break. He said the payroll lady near the yard office can explain why the deduction changed.
Fine, but write it down. You know they'll ask dates and last four numbers.
Already did. I have the March sheet beside me with the $3,435 number circled.
you going to that thing at the rec center sat? the one about the after school slots
yeah. they're saying they may cut Saturday hours and the kids over by the Pelican Landing apts got nowhere else to go
what they spending it on then
that's what I want to know. $84k for a consultant study before they even ask the mamas on Telephone Rd what they need. makes no sense
Mama wants them yeast rolls Sunday. don't show up empty handed
I got her. won't be over til after 3 though, Tues/Thurs runs late and I gotta catch up Wednesday
you and them books. mama was going on again how if she hadn't gone down sick that spring you'd have walked across that stage with the rest of em. she still carries it
wasn't on her. money wasn't there either, you remember. it is what it is. doing it now. fractions tomorrow, pray for me
Mama fell again. Not bad. Sitting up. But the home aide didn't show and I'm losing it.
Breathe. I'm pulling up the contact list. I'll get Cousin Bea over there in 20, call the agency, and reach Dr. Hammond's after-hours line. You stay with Mama.
Bea pulled up. Agency called back. How do you do this every time, Kail. I would've just been crying on the porch.
Because somebody has to dial. Tomorrow morning I'll redo the aide schedule so we never have an empty Thursday again.
Coming by after shift tomorrow. Anything left or should I grab my own?
Shift got pushed late. Can I crash on the sofa if I get there after 11?
There will be soup, rice, and the last of the greens from the garden. I can fry eggs if you are still hungry.
Yes, but fold the quilt back in the hall closet before church. Eli's little sheets are in that same stack.
That works. You still going to Pascagoula in the morning?
Only to pay the light bill and skip the shoe place. The other office can wait until they have a later slot.
Got it. Is Marissa bringing him tomorrow morning or Sunday?
Sunday unless her plans change. I saved you both some muffins.
How did the checkup go after choir practice?
Fine. The nurse had me fill those two little pages again, and Dr. Wilkes only fussed about sleep, caffeine, and making the bills wait till daylight.
Then tonight put the church supper names on one sheet and close the notebook before bed.
I will. If it is written out, it stops feeling like twelve loose things tugging at me.
Mrs. Avery is coming after all, but she sounded tired on the phone.
I will save her the end seat near the door and make a small container she can take home.
Do you need me to bring anything besides tea?
Tea is enough. I have the names beside the pans already, just need you to glance at the choir sign-up.
I saved you a plate from choir. Renee said you were still at Darlene's when practice started.
Had to match the morning row with the bottles she keeps moving. Then she needed bread and bananas.
I can bring the plate by and sit with her while you eat.
Just leave it on the porch if you're passing. I don't want you making another stop for me.
Mama says her arm still feels heavy. Did they tell y'all that was normal?
The nurse said ice pack and move it some. Same as when I did my two stops last fall.
I'll tell her. She keeps listening to Cousin Pam's mess.
I pulled the Mississippi Department of Health page too. It says call if fever stays high, otherwise give it a day.
Hit yet?
Just checked. In there
Good. Power and water going out today, $312 and $86. Leaving $40 in the truck envelope for you
Ok. Don't forget my back script pickup on the way back
You up? I get off at 8 and can stop by if you need lifting.
Already outside. Bring those bamboo stakes from the shed if you come.
For the red plants by the fence?
Yes, and grab the flat basket. I want the cucumbers off the vine before it warms up.
I can swing by after my shift. You still need me to try those two slices?
Yes. One has the darker syrup and one has the chopped pecans toasted first.
Cool. Also Ms. Carol at work asked if you wrote her name down for Friday.
I did. Her foil plate and Mr. James's deep dish are on the list, and I need the good boxes before then.
That warehouse form asks if family ever lived out of state for emergency contact history. What do I put for you?
Just use Moss Point. Before that was Mama's place, same county. Visits don't count.
It also has those little ancestry boxes. I don't know which one goes for our side.
Use the same one I mark at the clinic, and leave the origin question like mine unless your daddy tells you different.
Can I crash there after shift? Marcus is bringing people by my place and it'll be loud.
You can. Same rule as always: leave anything with a flame, foil, or mystery snacks in your car.
Yes ma'am. Just laundry and work boots.
Good. Sheets are clean and I made lemon bars from my own pan.
Eli asked if Nana works at a job. I told him you bake and you study. he said you should work where they have the puzzle rug
tell that boy the puzzle rug is at the rec center on Main and that is exactly where I am trying to land afternoons
Mama. for real? a paid thing or volunteering
paid. couple afternoons, maybe Saturdays. once the certificate is in hand I am walking in
Mama wants to know if you're driving her to the 11 o'clock tomorrow or the 8:30. She says the 8:30 lets her get home before her stories
11. Tommy's still wore out from Saturday and I want to sit through the whole service, not slip out at offering
Fine. I'll grab her after and bring her by your place for lunch. You doing the gumbo or the red beans
Red beans. Got the andouille from the Vancleave stand Thursday. Bring the cornbread pan back, mine walked off with Caleb
Mama wants you to bring biscuits tomorrow. Are you still on that toast change the nurse fussed about?
I can bring biscuits for them. I am packing my own wheat toast and boiled eggs.
Good. And do not nibble on Mama's coconut bars while you are standing there talking.
I know. I wrote the June recheck on the fridge so I behave myself.
For Mama's birthday lunch, do not let everybody hand you boxes just because you got there first.
I already told Tommy he has plates and ice. Caleb can move the folding tables when he comes.
Good. Put yourself by the side wall, not running between kitchen and porch.
That's the plan. I am bringing that padded chair from the sewing room too.
Put $25 cash in the blue envelope after gas. Don't let me forget.
I wrote it down. That gets us closer to one night near Gulf Shores if the motel price stays low.
One night is fine. You still wanting that stop by the old fort marker on the way?
If we leave early. I also found a Jackson County pension list that mentions a family name Mama used to say.
Do you still have that picture of me on the front steps with the pink backpack?
Yes, right after we got settled on this street. You had just started fourth grade.
I want Eli to see it. Also Daddy said the hallway floor still dips by the linen closet?
Same dip, new squeak. Tell him the house keeps adding noises but the bill keeps coming steady.
Mama wants to know if you can run her to the foot doctor Wednesday at 4.
Not Wednesday. You know I cannot be late getting to the church, Pat does not start without me on the alto side and I am not leaving them stuck.
Lord, every Wednesday with you. Fine I will take her. Move it to Tuesday next time.
Tuesday or Thursday works. Just not Wednesday evenings, ever.
You watching the debate panel right now? They're going at it about the school board thing.
Cut it off after about ten minutes. They were just talking over each other, I couldn't tell what either one actually said.
Well Cousin Trey shared a post saying the new superintendent already decided to cut bus routes. You hear anything?
Not from anywhere I'd repeat yet. I'll see what the Sun Herald says tomorrow. Don't go telling Mama that before we know.
Can you swing Mama to the foot doctor Wednesday at 10? I can't get off.
Yeah, my Wednesday is open this week. Only Thursday I've got the church kitchen 1 to 4.
See, that's why I asked you and not Cousin Pam. Your week looks like nothing on paper and somehow ends up at 8 hours.
Closer to 9 this week with the supper sign-up. Next week's worse, Easter prep starts.
Tomorrow's 6:40 circle is still on. Cheryl said she can only do one lap if the air feels like it did today.
One lap may be plenty. I am not doing the cemetery road unless several of us are there.
Fair. I'll park beside you and we can keep to the church side where the trees cover most of it.
That works. I need the early time or I will talk myself out of it.
Pastor wants to know if you'll lead the supply drive again at the August meeting. He said no one knows where everything is but you.
Tell him yes. Same as every year since 05. I already started my own tub this week so I'm in the rhythm.
Of course you did. Twenty one years and you still treat August like it's around the corner in March.
After what we saw nobody on this coast gets to be casual about it. I told Marissa the same thing when she moved to Ocean Springs. You start in March, you don't scramble in July.
mama's washer is making that noise again. repair guy quoted 380 if it's the pump
lord. can we split it between us? if i pull 380 out of our account this week it eats almost everything we set aside
i can do half. don't drain yall's cushion for this, hurricane season ain't far off and that roof patch is still on yall's list
thank you. half is doable. i'd rather keep something behind us in case tommy's back acts up or the truck does something
Mama's lady at the senior center is running her mouth about that yard sign on Dolores's fence. wants to know which side we're on
tell her I voted Tuesday and that's between me and the booth. I'm not putting a sign in my grass for either one
you sound like Daddy. he wouldn't tell us either
faith, take care of your own, don't spend what you don't have. the rest is between me and the Lord. I'll do the cake walk at the supper but I won't wear nobody's t-shirt
Booster mailer came today. Tiger season pass went up to $90 a seat this year
Renewing both? Last fall we held one for Caleb when he came up after his shifts
Two on the home side, same row as before. I'll cut the check friday after the bills clear
Good. Field's been holding up better since they redid the drainage after the river backed up last spring
Mom your event post popped up on my feed. The one with the donation drive.
Good share it if you can. I tagged the choir group and the Moss Point cleanup group.
Did. Miss Carolyn from your old job asked me how to sign up, she said she does not see your posts anymore.
Tell her I will call her tonight after supper. Her number is still the same one right.
How did Dr. Laird go yesterday? Eli asked if Nana got a sticker too.
No sticker, but he was pleased with the numbers I wrote down. Same tiny tablet, no changes.
Good. Did they give you another date?
September 22 at 10:15. I put it in before I walked out.
Did you see what Kenneth shared about the school board vote? You need to tell him that is not what happened in that meeting.
Renee. No.
He's our cousin, somebody has to. You actually went to the meeting.
I'm not getting into it with Kenneth in writing where everybody can see. If he calls me I'll tell him plain. I'm not putting that on my page.
Fine. But you sat reading those comments a good while, I could see when you went quiet.
Choir wanting to know if you can swap to Thursday morning practice next month
Can't do mornings honey. That's my sit-down day with the planner and the envelopes before Tommy's check lands
Right right, I keep forgetting Fridays are sacred over there
Once a month I'm running close to $3,000 by the time I'm done. Need my coffee and quiet for it
Eli asked tonight why the policeman on TV was yelling at the man on the ground. I didn't know what to say.
Oh baby. Tell him most of them help people, like Officer Pritchett who came when y'all locked the keys in the car. But some of them get loud too fast and that ain't right either.
Should we even have the news on with him in the room?
I'd turn it off when he's there and y'all talk about it after. That's how we always done it. Just at the kitchen table, not making a whole big thing of it.
Saw Miss Bernice at Winn-Dixie. She still asks about Mama. Said she remembered her steam table line on chicken day.
Lord, Mama ran that line for what, 20 some years? Bernice was a lunch lady at the middle school same time.
Both of them on their feet all day for that district check. I don't know how Mama did it with us two and Granny in the house.
She just did. Daddy on the yard shift, her at the school. Granny watching us when the hours overlapped.
Mama said you left greens and tomatoes on her porch. Did you save any for your own house?
Yes ma'am, I kept enough for supper. Tommy can grill chicken and I will slice what came in this morning.
Good. And do your circle with Linda before you come fussing over Mama's pill box tonight.
Already planned for 5:40. I behave better after a few rounds and a little talking.
You want me to grab milk on the way in?
Yes, half gallon is enough. I already pulled two chops from the freezer.
Need dog food or anything from that aisle?
No, skip that aisle. Just milk and the small trash bags for our bathroom.
You sitting down with the notebook already? Need to ask you something about Mama's pills

events.title: Local room before supper

events.title: Kitchen table numbers

events.title: Fabric table

events.title: Alto rehearsal - First Baptist fellowship hall
events.notes: Bring the maroon folder. Sister Geneva wants us 10 min early to run the Easter cantata bridge.

events.title: Call Gulf Coast Servicing
events.notes: Ask about escrow letter before Friday draft; Tommy has pay stub in truck. Check porch quote folder from the 2008 closing box.

events.title: Call Miss Earlene, Mr. Bobby, Sister Pat re Saturday cleanup
events.notes: Earlene 228-475 line, Bobby cell only rings between 11 and 1, Pat prefers landline. Confirm ride for Earlene with Renee.

events.title: GED practice — math section 4
events.notes: finish word problems, time the reading passage, bring the highlighter that actually works

events.title: Ward 4 town hall - drainage on Griffin Ave
events.notes: bring the photos from Mrs. Beasley's yard after the Feb rain. ask if Pastor Ray and the two new neighbors from Pecan St got the time right. don't let Councilman Hardy run the whole hour again.

events.title: Friday sit-down at kitchen table
events.notes: Wait for Tommy's deposit to clear. Pull planner + green notebook. Sort envelopes: groceries, gas, power, water, cell, church. Carry leftover from last week into grocery envelope.

events.title: Church fish fry prep and serving
events.notes: Bring two folding chairs from home. Ask Caleb to unload drink coolers before 5:00. Mark 6:20 and 7:10 for ten-minute pauses in choir room.

events.title: Friday bills after Tommy deposit clears
events.notes: Use $3,435 working number for March. Set aside truck gas, light bill, clinic copay, and groceries before ordering Caleb's tires.

events.title: Linda - east lot loops, then beds
events.location: First Baptist east parking lot; home raised beds after
events.notes: Bring small bag for Renee: collards, green onions, 3 tomatoes if ripe.

events.title: Mardi Gras parade route walkthrough - Krewe of Gautier
events.location: Howard Ave between 4th and 9th, Moss Point
events.notes: Confirm parking cones for the church lot, food tent placement, and 14 sign-up slots for water and tea. Bring the binder. Settle the dispute between the Riverside ladies and the choir auxiliary over who gets the corner tent before it gets ugly.

events.title: Storm shelf check
events.notes: Count bottled water, flashlights, batteries, canned soup, Tommy's work gloves, my charger pack. Put Caleb's borrowed cooler by back door if he texts about fishing.

events.title: Early oven notes before church
events.notes: Half pan berry filling; 8 drop biscuits with White Lily; pecan filling test in small shell. Label samples A/B and send two covered plates with Caleb.

events.title: Before service: kitchen list + choir folder
events.location: First Baptist fellowship hall, Moss Point
events.notes: Bring foil pans, serving spoons, paper labels, alto folder, and extra rolls. Check Mrs. Avery's table before sitting down.

events.title: Sunday lunch - set extra plates
events.notes: High chair from closet, 4T rain jacket by back door, send Caleb home with red beans if he stops after warehouse.

events.title: Pine Grove Spring Sing-Along - Magnolia Park
events.notes: Saw the event flyer on the Jackson County happenings page through the choir group, RSVP'd yes. Mae forwarded a 'cancelled' screenshot Saturday - called the church office before I passed it on, still on. Folding chairs in the truck, Tommy may grill after.

events.title: Call list before errands
events.notes: Ask Bayou Dental for a May opening. Check pantry before Greer's: rice, soup cans, eggs. Leave Shoe Station pickup for later.

events.title: Jackson County clinic stop + pharmacy counter

events.notes: Bring insurance card, COVID card, and the yellow slip from the nurse. Ask pharmacist whether flu record shows on the printout.

events.title: Bring folder for county form
events.notes: Need license, old Bible card, Mama's family names, and the checked boxes from last year's clinic sheet.

events.title: Air out porch cushions before Sunday
events.notes: Move metal can off side table, wash quilt, set tea pitcher inside only. Use labeled pantry desserts for family.

events.title: Singing River clinic follow-up

events.notes: Bring March lab sheet. Ask about the 5.8 note, breakfast swaps, and whether June repeat is still needed.

events.title: Food bank pickup + sort - Fellowship Hall

events.notes: Tuesday rotation. Bring the clipboard from Sunday. Drop boxes at Mrs. Halpern's after.

events.title: WLOX 6 + supper
events.notes: national at 6:30 — keep volume low, mute if they start hollering over each other again

events.title: Rotate blue tub + restock folder

events.title: Launch w/ Tommy & Caleb
events.notes: Cooler, ice, live shrimp, two rods, tackle box. Sandwiches from home. Back before noon so Tommy can rest his back.

events.title: Drive Mama to Griffin St cousins cookout

events.title: Sunday lunch — Marissa, Eli, Caleb
